seed_ledger.name: PowerConneX I and II New Albany Energy Center
seed_ledger.reason: EXISTING_ROW. The Reporting Project (July 2026) says The Energy Cooperative is building a 24 inch, 24 mile, 160 million dollar pipeline paid for by PowerConneX to fuel the 216 MW plant for the EdgeConneX New Albany data center. First gas comes from a TC Energy line near Granville and phase 2 ties to the Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage line near Hebron. The cooperative's own page lists up to 500 MMcf per day and behind-the-meter power for an off-grid data center. This is roster row P8320, Licking County Pipeline. Tag it as a data center lead. How plant I (the smaller unit) gets gas is unconfirmed: only an aggregator says the cooperative's system. Searches run: 9. Sources checked: the Reporting Project July 2026 article (names PowerConneX, 216 MW, route and phases); the Reporting Project March 2026 article (proposal); the cooperative's project page (size and pressure); the New Albany city natural gas page (easement outreach); Cleanview report (aggregator, lead only); Ohio siting board dockets for the two plants (no readable gas details); EdgeConneX project page.

evidence.note: names PowerConneX, the 216 MW plant and the cooperative's 24 inch pipeline
cooperative project page for the Licking County pipeline, 24 miles, 24 inch, 500 MMcf per day
